messages:
alex: Heads-up — I'm proposing a 'minimal delta' packaging playbook for on-prem upgrades. Goal: ship the smallest signed delta that still gives us a safe rollback path and quick verification on air-gapped devices.

liz: Curious — what does "minimal" mean here? bytes, components, or update surface?

alex: Primarily bytes + component scope. Idea is to compute a dependency-aware delta (component-level) instead of full image diffs, sign the delta manifest, and include an idempotent revert plan.

morgan: Love the small-updates idea. Questions: how do we handle cross-component ordering? e.g., schema changes that require a two-step DB migration?

alex: Great point. Proposal: delta manifests include an ordered op list with explicit pre/post hooks. Operator must be able to run pre-hooks in a safe sandbox. If any hook fails, we stop and surface a clear rollback marker.

sam: For airgap, verification time matters. We can’t pull large artifact chains. Suggest including a short verification vector in the manifest: checksums + a small Merkle proof of changed blobs so devices can verify without fetching everything.

rachel: Merkle proofs sound heavy to implement client-side. Maybe we can ship a compact index that points to changed artifact chunks and a single signature over that index?

alex: Yes — compact index + signature is the pragmatic path. Merkle optional for customers wanting provable minimal fetch. Default: signed compact index + per-blob checksums.

pete: How do we expose this in the operator UI/CLI? Users will want a dry-run and an offline verify step.

liz: UX: `redwoodctl preview-apply --manifest <file>` should validate indexes, run pre-hooks in dry-run mode, and produce a human-friendly checklist.

eng-sre: From SRE standpoint, we need deterministic failure signals. Propose embedding a small state machine in the manifest: states = [pending, applied, verifying, failed, rolled-back]. The agent must persist state to a local journal so incomplete upgrades can resume.

alex: Agree. Journaling is critical. Also recommend using a lease mechanism: apply window + operator confirmation for risky deltas. If lease expires, agent auto-aborts and marks manifest as stale.

sam: What about keys? For on-prem we already have customer KMS/HSM options. Should deltas be signed by Redwood CA only, or allow customer signing?

rachel: Offer both. Default: Redwood-signed with included cert chain. Enterprise: customer-signed artifacts (we verify chain against customer's root). Need clear UI for trust decisions.

morgan: Rollback plan detail: must be symmetric to apply plan. Are we storing inverse ops in the manifest or relying on artifact archive?

alex: We store lightweight inverse ops for simple changes and reference an archived snapshot for big reversions. For example, config files: inverse ops present. For large binaries: manifest references the previous artifact snapshot ID (small metadata entry, not whole blob).

liz: Archive retention will be a policy knob (e.g., retain last N snapshots). We should warn operators if a delta relies on an archived snapshot that has expired.

pete: Testing: how do we validate rollback in CI for on-prem? Need a canned failure injection mode so operator can run a simulated bad hook and ensure the inverse path works.

alex: Add `--simulate-failure` to the CLI. Also recommend CI job that runs delta apply + simulated failure + automated rollback and verifies idempotency. Keep that as a release gating check for packaging toolchain.

eng-sre: Observability: emit compact events to the control plane (when available) and always keep a local compact trace with hashes so auditors can reconstruct the timeline in air-gapped cases.

sam: Performance: small devices might struggle with heavy signature verification. We should support two signature profiles: fast (ed25519) and legacy (rsa) depending on device capabilities.

rachel: Note for compliance: when customers bring their own signing keys, we need to support key rotation with grace windows and preserve ability to verify older signed manifests.

alex: Implementation plan (rough):
- v1: compact index + signed manifest, pre/post hook model, journaling, lease-based apply window.
- v2: optional Merkle proofs, customer-signed deltas, CI failure-simulate workflows.
- v3: incremental binary patching (bsdiff-like) and on-host patch streaming for low-bandwidth.

liz: Any blockers? Ops and eng-sre should review audit + retention requirements. Also need a small shim on the agent to handle inverse ops and simulate-failure flags.

eng-sre: Will put together compliance checklist and retention ROIs. One ask: manifest size MUST be < 64KB by default (excluding checksums) to keep agent memory small. If >64KB, agent warns and requires explicit operator override.

pete: Can we have a canonical example manifest in the repo with comments? That will speed onboarding.

alex: Yep — I'll draft an example with a config-update, small binary replace, and a simulated failing hook. Expect PR early next week.

deploy-bot: Deploy note: no production changes scheduled. Reminder: run upgrade-sim job in staging after PR lands. :white_check_mark:

morgan: One more thought — fallback strategies for partial success (some components applied, others failed). We should prefer partial roll-forward with compatible fallbacks instead of blind rollback when safe. Manifest needs to mark components as independently reversible vs. globally transactional.

alex: Good call. We'll add a `transactional: boolean` flag per-manifest and `component.transactional` per-component. Default: component-level fallbacks to keep uptime.

rachel: Thanks — this reads like a pragmatic plan. If we keep the manifest format compact and the agent invariant checks strict, customers should get both safety and small updates.

alex: Thanks everyone. Next steps: I'll open RFC PR with example manifests, CLI proposals, and a proposed agent state journal format. Please flag any non-negotiable compliance items in the PR review.

liz: +1

morgan: +1

sam: +1

rachel: +1
